key_clause.text: a government entity may not grant legal personhood to, nor recognize legal personhood in: (1) artificial intelligence; (2) an inanimate object; (3) a body of water; (4) land; (5) real property; (6) atmospheric gases; (7) an astronomical object; (8) weather; (9) a plant; (10) a nonhuman animal; or (11) any other member of a taxonomic domain that is not a human being

bills.provenance: Seeded from Smith, Caviola & Alexander (2026), Table 1, Figure 2 and 'Laws and Bills Cited'
bills.notes: VERIFIED against the enrolled text 2026-08-10. Enacts Utah Code ch. 63G-31. Eleven enumerated categories; 'human being' is defined as 'a member of the species classified as Homo sapiens', which is the taxonomic anchor. 'Legal personhood' is defined to cover BOTH the rights/obligations of an individual AND of 'a person other than an individual', i.e. it reaches juridical personhood - relevant to the zero-member LLC question. 'Governmental entity' includes a court, the Legislature, and bodies with adjudicatory or rulemaking authority. Bars only granting NEW personhood, so needs no corporate saving clause. Triggered Ban v. Utah (NhRP), dismissed May 2025. Senate sponsor Don L. Ipson is not named in the paper.

key_clause.text: 'Person,' 'interested person,' 'member of the public,' and any other similar terms referring to those who may engage with governmental agencies under this division do not include artificial intelligence systems, autonomous agents, robots, or other nonhuman entities, whether physical or digital.

bills.provenance: Seeded from Smith, Caviola & Alexander (2026), Table 1, Figure 2 and 'Laws and Bills Cited'
bills.notes: VERIFIED 2026-08-10. STATUS MOVED SINCE THE PAPER: amended in the Assembly 25 June 2026, i.e. past the Senate. Operative text is BROADER than the paper describes - it excludes 'artificial intelligence systems, autonomous agents, robots, or other nonhuman entities, whether physical or digital', not AI alone. Reaches 12 code sections across the Government Code and Public Resources Code. Coauthors span both parties (Jones and Ochoa Bogh are Republicans), supporting the paper's 'primarily though not exclusively Democratic' characterisation.

bills.notes: VERIFIED 2026-08-10. The operative bar sits at s 22612(d)(5)(G): a companion chatbot may not claim it 'is sentient, conscious, or human'.
